featured_reviews.name: Jayashri Devadhar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Having heard reviews about this tiny but interesting joint at Charni Road serving Locho, we decided to go there a few days ago. Needless to say, it was extremely tiny with seating for just 5 people at max.

The menu showed pizzas, wraps, fries and a few other stuff too along with a wide variety of Locho but we decided to go with what the place is known for. Everything in the menu, we were told, could be made Jain, except for what was expressly named as containing garlic. We tried the basic oil Locho and butter garlic Locho, both of which were good and quite distinct in taste. I would give the butter locho a slightly upper hand for its flavours and along with the Sev on top and chopped onion and green chutney served alongside, it tasted delicious. Would surely come back again for it when Locho cravings strike back!

featured_reviews.name: Anmol Sanyasi
featured_reviews.review_text:
We went to Flavors at Bay near Hotel Hira mainly because it was convenient for us. Unfortunately, the food was a big disappointment.

I understand that it’s a vegetarian restaurant and spices are an important part of Indian cooking, but spices should complement the meal — not completely overpower it. Everything we ordered tasted like it was just packed with masala and nothing else.

We ordered momos, and they were honestly the worst part of the meal. They didn’t taste like real momos at all. Instead of a proper filling, it felt like a dough ball stuffed with pure spices. The taste matched how it looked — just overwhelming masala with no balance. Coming from a Nepali background where we eat momos often, this was really disappointing.

The biryani was the same story. It was mostly spice with very little flavor or balance beyond that.

The service itself was good and the staff were polite. The location was convenient for us as well. However, the restaurant felt quite empty and overall the food experience was not good. Unfortunately, the heavy spices even gave us heartburn afterwards.

We really wanted to enjoy the meal, but it ended up being a very disappointing experience.

The ambience is clean, calm, and perfect for both family dinners and casual outings. The staff is polite, attentive, and ensures quick service without compromising on quality. Every dish we tried was well-prepared, delicious, and beautifully presented.

What I really appreciated is their commitment to Jain food preparation standards while still maintaining rich taste and variety. The desserts were also a great highlight!

Overall, a fantastic place for anyone looking for pure veg and Jain cuisine with great taste and a pleasant dining atmosphere. Highly recommended for family meals and special occasions.

Looking at this behaviour, i will not like to even like to recommend this place to anyone.

featured_reviews.name: Burjiz
featured_reviews.review_text:
Golden Chimney offered a comfortable and enjoyable dining experience during our visit.

The ambience inside the restaurant was quite good, especially after entering from the outside summer heat into the air-conditioned seating area.

There happened to be an IPL match playing during the visit as well, which added a lively atmosphere without making the place feel too noisy or chaotic.

For drinks, I ordered a fresh lime water, which was refreshing and suited the weather well.

For starters, we ordered the Murgh Lasoni Tikka and Classic Chicken Chilly. Both dishes were enjoyable, though the Murgh Lasoni Tikka stood out more for its flavour and preparation.

For the mains, we had the Butter Chicken, which was well prepared and satisfying.

Service was good, seating was comfortable, and overall the restaurant provided a pleasant dine-in experience.

All in all, a good restaurant option in the Opera House / Lamington Road area for a relaxed lunch or dinner with decent food and ambience.

featured_reviews.name: Anmol Sanyasi
featured_reviews.review_text:
From the very first meal, Golden Chimney completely won us over. The food is absolutely delicious — every dish is rich in flavor, beautifully balanced, and full of authentic taste. You can truly taste Mumbai in the food — the spices, the freshness, and the variety all come together perfectly. Each bite felt thoughtfully prepared and full of character.
What made our experience even more special was the staff. They are incredibly gentle, kind, and genuinely thoughtful. The hospitality here stands out. They pay attention to every detail and make sure you feel comfortable and taken care of. Whether it was helping us choose dishes or checking in to make sure everything was perfect, their service was warm and sincere. We were visiting Mumbai from outside the city for just four days, and we ended up eating at Golden Chimney four out of five days — that says everything. When you find a place that combines amazing food with outstanding hospitality, you naturally want to return. Every time we came back, the quality was consistent and impressive.
The money we spent was absolutely worth it.
The portion sizes, the flavor, the cleanliness, and the service all reflect great value for the price.
It's rare to find a restaurant where both the food and the people leave such a lasting impression.
If you're in Mumbai and want authentic, flavorful food with heartfelt hospitality, Golden Chimney is a must-visit. We will definitely return the next time we are in the city.

The Paneer Schezwan Khepsa Rice was packed with flavor, perfectly spicy, and loaded with delicious paneer pieces. The Manchurian Chatpata was crispy, tangy, and a perfect starter. featured_reviews.review_text: Visited Mao Family Restaurant for lunch and tried the Hungama Kepsa (half) — good portion size and flavorful, definitely worth it. The Chicken Tandoori was outstanding; juicy, well-marinated, and something I would surely recommend to any non-vegetarian.However, the vegetarian menu was a huge disappointment. The Paneer Kepsa tasted more like a Chinese-style gravy than authentic Kepsa, and the Paneer Crispy was neither crispy nor made from real paneer — it was clearly synthetic. At ₹265, the quantity and quality of paneer were unacceptable.In short, this place is a delight for non-vegetarians but a nightmare for vegetarians.

featured_reviews.name: bhavika jethwa
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Mao Restaurant and had an incredible dining experience! I ordered the Chicken Noorani Kabab and Chicken Tikka Mini Kepsa, and I must say, the kababs were absolutely delicious. They had a delightful tandoori coating, and the filling was made of perfectly spiced seekh chicken. The spice level was just right—medium spicy, which added to the overall flavor without overwhelming the palate.

What made it even more special was that it was served on a sizzling plate, enhancing the presentation and aroma. The Chicken Tikka Mini Kepsa was a unique addition to the menu, and being the first place to serve it definitely earned them some extra points. The taste was simply amazing, and each bite was a burst of flavor.

I would highly recommend Mao Restaurant to anyone looking for a great meal. The combination of delicious food, unique offerings, and excellent presentation makes it a must-visit spot. Can't wait to go back and try more dishes!

I would never give the review or recommend this place to any one, On 17/04/2026, my friends and I visited the restaurant for dinner. After finishing our meal, we stepped outside and were waiting for a cab when one of my friends suddenly collapsed due to low blood pressure and fainted right outside your restaurant.

In that moment of urgency, I approached your staff requesting a small amount of sugar to help revive her. However, I was shocked by their response—they bluntly said they do not keep sugar. What was even more surprising was that at the same time, sugar was clearly available in the mukhwas kept there.

It was a matter of basic human kindness, and such a small help could have made a big difference in that situation. Unfortunately, the staff showed complete lack of empathy and humanity.

This is particularly disappointing because Kalbadevi has always been a place we frequently visit for lunch and dinner. Experiencing such insensitive behavior from your team was unexpected and unacceptable.

I do have a video of the incident, I will upload it soon. I will Raise a complaint too.

featured_reviews.name: Roshani Batra
featured_reviews.review_text:
A perfect family dining place to indulge in a lot of varieties from their special multi-cuisine menu varieties. Its a whole paradise of scrumptuous meal to choose from while the family can have a special time bonding and eating lovely food out here. They offer Gujarati, Punjabi, Chinese, South indian and even limited mexican and lebanese options too alongwith the traditional Mumbai style food. Dessert and beverage options are limited. I could see beautiful families chilling and the vibrant ambiance to spend a happy time. Everything came out to be too warm and welcoming. The staff was very friendly providing you your order in no time. According to my experience, khana khazana is more of Indian food rather chinese or mexican or any other (not indian) dishes that they offer, so 1 would recommend to only opt for Indian food and you could know why from my below mentioned food experience-
My dinner experience was a mix of Chinese, Gujarati and Punjabi dishes. I had chinese and gujarati as my starters and went for punjabi as the main course. My orders were-
• Veg Mushroom Soup- This was very nice; had loads of mushroom and veggies just like hot & sour.
• Sweet Corn Soup- This was too sweet, the proper taste of authentic sweet corn soup was not here.
• Veg Manchurian- This had more of soya sauce present in the manchurian.
• Paneer chilly- Atleast paneer was crispy, again the same had soya sauce more.
• Masala Fried Khichia- Just loved this authentic Gujarati option. This had liads of veggies, butter, green chutney and crispiness to bite on.
• Deewana Mastana- A punjabi dish option highly recommended- basically its a mix of two veggies.

• Kaju Khazana- This had kaju and garlic. Will go well with kulcha or roti.
• Cheese garlic naan & butter kulcha- Good
• Caramel Custard- This one's my favourite. Must try if you wanna go for a dessert. This was their dessert of the day.
• Chocolate mousse- Dessert of the day turned out to be delicious for a chocolate lover.
Rich Indian food and cosy environment are what I would look for in this place. The vibe is warm and a must for family dining and Indian food.

This is a 15 year old restaurant serving pure veg food with indian cuisine and they have even started with chinese,mexican and italian as well. The place is a 5 min walking distance from charni road station. The staff was good Nd helped us with suggesting the food.

Veg schezwan fingers was a chinese based starter it had minced vegges deep fried and topped with schezwan sauce. This was also good in taste.

For main course
Veg Deewana mastana which had 2 subzis in it one was yellow based gravy which had paneer cheese and veggies in it.
The other one was a red based gravy with chopped veggies it had right amount of spices and flavours.

Veg handi biryani it was a red based biryani and damn it was too goood. It was served with papad.

For deserts
Chocolate mousse dont miss this one of the best mousse ive tried. The chocolaty taste was perfect just loved it.

The sweet lassi is also amazing and thick they dont use water it was purely made of curd. Totally worth a visit
